report.summary: Chunk 6 of reach.py: defines _branch_payload, _iter_funcs, _collect_funcs, _is_forever, _scan_dynamic, _resolve, _package_parents; includes docstrings and comments with checkable claims.
risks: _scan_dynamic | medium | Non-literal argument to import_module/__import__ is recorded as a dynamic site; the comment says it's a 'hole in the static picture' but the code does not verify that the argument is actually a string or that the call is to the correct function. | Check that the function name check is sufficient and that the lineno attribute exists.

_package_parents | low | The function assumes known_rels contains paths with forward slashes; if rel uses backslashes or is a dotted name, the split will be incorrect. | Verify input format consistency.

handoff.purpose: Define functions for collecting function-level imports, dynamic imports, and resolving package parent relationships.

symbols.name: _branch_payload
symbols.note: Returns a list of two tuples: ('records', tuple of import records) and ('names', tuple of referenced names and attributes) from the body of an if node.

symbols.name: _iter_funcs
symbols.note: Generator that yields (qualified_name, function_node) for every FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef in the AST, recursing into nested functions and classes.

symbols.name: _collect_funcs
symbols.note: Populates src.func_records, src.func_names, src.func_loops, and src.func_calls by iterating over all functions in the tree.

symbols.name: _is_forever
symbols.note: Returns True if the node is a While loop with a constant True test.

symbols.name: _DOTTED_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching a dotted Python identifier (e.g., 'foo.bar.baz').

symbols.name: _scan_dynamic
symbols.note: Scans the AST for calls to import_module or __import__; if the first argument is a string literal, adds it to src.dyn_targets; otherwise records the location in src.dynamic.

symbols.name: _resolve
symbols.note: Resolves a set of relative paths from import records, using resolve_python_imports and a dotted-to-relative mapping.

symbols.name: _package_parents
symbols.note: Returns a list of __init__.py paths that are parents of the given relative path, limited to those in known_rels.

claims.text: orelse is deliberately excluded: for an elif chain the orelse IS the next branch, and folding it in would credit every subcommand with every later subcommand's imports.
claims.why: The function only processes node.body and does not include node.orelse, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: A literal argument is a REAL edge and is treated as one. A non-literal one is a hole in the static picture; it is recorded so the report can say a module is unknown instead of accusing it of being an island.
claims.why: The code adds literal string arguments to src.dyn_targets and records non-literal arguments with file and line number in src.dynamic.

claims.text: ``__init__.py`` files Python imports as a side effect of importing this module. These edges are real at runtime -- omitting them would report a package's ``__init__`` as an island whenever nothing imports it by name.
claims.why: The function constructs parent __init__.py paths and includes them if they are in known_rels.

observations.what: _scan_dynamic uses ast.Attribute check for fn.attr == 'import_module' but does not check the object; e.g., something.import_module would be caught regardless of the object.
_package_parents splits rel by '/' and assumes it is a forward-slash path; if rel is a dotted name, the split will not produce expected parent paths.

The comment 'every import, at every scope depth -- this is where lazy CLI branch imports live' is not directly verifiable in this chunk; it describes behavior of _collect_funcs which scans all functions.
